fragments.text: we should check and see whether we are ahead of Rob's upstream master or vice versa

reply_text:
㊥ (gist) We're well ahead, and Rob hasn't pushed anything since our last push to him. His `main` (electric-samurai/mfuton-share) is still at `8c5a3146`, the merge codex-4 pushed with your OK on 10-05 at 02:58. `claude-4/cand-1` has **150 commits** his main doesn't have. His main has **6 commits** that cand-1 lacks.

🈖 (what the 6 are) They aren't new work from Rob:
- One is his: `049047a1` (10-01), "Reconcile Lean parser/compiler Python closure".
- The other five are our own integration commits from the 10-04/05 merge into his main. That merge brought his reconcile commit in, plus the fixes needed to make it fit.

Those five never came back into cand-1, so cand-1 has never had Rob's reconcile commit. The difference is 89 files, about 7,600 lines, mostly his closure work plus our adjustments.

㊟ (two consequences)
1. **Rob's main is from before the regression.** It was cut from cand-1 on 10-05 before the stop-C merge broke isNone, and it was pushed with "20/20 cold MATCH". So his agents are running code that's still good on those rows. The regression exists only on our side.
2. **Merging back.** Before our next push to Rob, cand-1 should merge `origin/main` back in, so his reconcile commit and our five adjustments are in cand-1. Otherwise the next push repeats the 10-04 merge work. Push to origin is disabled in config, and pushing to Rob stays your call.

🈰 (meanwhile) codex-36 is mapping atEnd, and the 21-row sweep at the cand-1 tip will show how many rows the regression costs. I'd do the back-merge after that, so a regression measured on cand-1 isn't mixed up with anything new coming in from Rob's side.
